title: Nonlinear parabolic compactness and monotone evolution

items.title: Banach evolution triples and weak time derivatives
items.statement:
Let $V$ be a separable reflexive real Banach space, let $H$ be a real Hilbert
space, and let $i:V\to H$ be an injective continuous linear map with dense
range. Let $V^*$ be the continuous real dual of $V$ and write
$\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle_{V^*,V}$ for its pairing with $V$. The canonical
map $J:H\to V^*$ is
$$J h(v)=(h,iv)_H\qquad(h\in H,\ v\in V).$$
It is continuous because $|Jh(v)|\le \|h\|_H\|i\|\|v\|_V$, and injective
because $i(V)$ is dense in $H$. A triple $(V,H,J)$ with these properties is
a **Banach evolution triple**. If $V$ is Hilbert, this is the real evolution
triple of [[def-parabolic-evolution-triple-and-energy-space]].

For $1<p<\infty$, $L^p(0,T;V)$ denotes the Bochner space of strongly
measurable $V$-valued functions with finite $p$th power norm, and
$p'=p/(p-1)$. For $u\in L^p(0,T;V)$ and $g\in L^{p'}(0,T;V^*)$, say
$g=u'$ in the distributional time sense if
$$\int_0^T (iu(t),iv)_H\,\phi'(t)\,dt =-\int_0^T\langle g(t),v\rangle_{V^*,V}\,\phi(t)\,dt$$
for every $v\in V$ and $\phi\in C_c^\infty(0,T)$. Define
$$W_p(0,T;V)=\{u\in L^p(0,T;V):u'\in L^{p'}(0,T;V^*)\}.$$
This definition assigns no endpoint values; a separate chain-rule theorem is
needed before evaluating a function in this space at an endpoint.
items.strategy: Extend the published Hilbert evolution-triple convention to a separable reflexive Banach energy space and specify every pairing and weak derivative.

references.title: Tomáš Roubíček, Nonlinear Partial Differential Equations with Applications, 2nd ed., Birkhäuser, 2005
references.locator: §7.2, evolution spaces and the H-valued trace, printed pp. 204–207

references.title: Christian Clason, Introduction to Finite Element Methods, lecture notes, arXiv:1709.08618v2

items.title: The subcritical W0 one p embedding into L2
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $d\ge1$, let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ be a bounded open set, and let $1<p<\infty$ satisfy $p>\max(1,2d/(d+2))$. Then $W_0^{1,p}(\Omega)$ is continuously and compactly embedded in $L^2(\Omega)$. In particular, the inclusion is dense. No boundary regularity is required.
items.strategy: Split p<d from p≥d; use the exact strict subcritical exponent in the first branch and finite-measure Lp-to-L2 continuity after Rellich in the second.

references.title: Haim Brezis, Functional Analysis, Sobolev Spaces and Partial Differential Equations, Springer Universitext, 2011
references.locator: Theorem 9.16, Rellich–Kondrachov, PDF pp. 299–300; local bounded-open reduction is proved below.

references.title: Tomáš Roubíček, Nonlinear Partial Differential Equations with Applications, 2nd ed., Birkhäuser, 2005
references.locator: §7.3, compact Sobolev embeddings in evolution compactness; this URL is historically dropped in batch coverage and is not used as a premise.

items.title: Time translations and mollification in Bochner Lp
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice.

Let $X$ be a real Banach space, $0<T<\infty$, and $1\le p<\infty$. For
$f\in L^p(0,T;X)$, translations are continuous in $L^p$ on every compact
subinterval of $(0,T)$. Convolution with a scalar smooth approximate identity
therefore converges to $f$ in $L^p$ on such subintervals. If $\mathcal P_k$
are interval partitions of $[0,T]$ with maximum cell length tending to zero,
the piecewise-constant interval averages of $f$ converge to $f$ in
$L^p(0,T;X)$.
items.strategy: Approximate by finite-valued simple functions, use scalar Lp translation continuity componentwise, then Minkowski and density.

references.title: Tomáš Roubíček, Nonlinear Partial Differential Equations with Applications, 2nd ed., Birkhäuser, 2005
references.locator: §7.2, smoothing of evolution-space functions; §7.3, time mollification in the Aubin–Lions proof

references.title: Christian Clason, Introduction to Finite Element Methods, lecture notes, arXiv:1709.08618v2
references.locator: Chapter 11 §11.1, PDF pp. 96–98, evolution-space approximation by time mollification

items.title: The zero-boundary W1p space is separable and reflexive
items.statement:
Assume the ultrafilter lemma, Dependent Choice and Hahn–Banach. Let
$\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ be bounded and open, $d\ge1$, and let
$1<p<\infty$. Then $W_0^{1,p}(\Omega;\mathbb R)$, with the norm inherited
from $W^{1,p}(\Omega;\mathbb R)$, is a separable reflexive real Banach space.
items.strategy: Use the closed-subspace theorem for reflexivity; embed W1p isometrically into a finite product of Lp spaces, restrict rational box-step approximants, then use a countable base to obtain separability of its subspace W0p.

references.title: Haim Brezis, Functional Analysis, Sobolev Spaces and Partial Differential Equations, Springer Universitext, 2011
references.locator: Proposition 9.1 and its pointer to the complete proof of Proposition 8.1, printed pp. 204 and 263; $W^{1,p}$ is Banach, reflexive for $1<p<\infty$, and separable for finite $p$.

items.title: Bochner Lp is complete for a Banach value space
items.statement:
Let $X$ be a real Banach space, $0<T<\infty$, and $1\le p<\infty$. Then
$L^p(0,T;X)$, with norm
$\|f\|_{L^p(X)}=(\int_0^T\|f(t)\|_X^pdt)^{1/p}$, is complete under Countable
Choice.
items.strategy: Choose a rapidly Cauchy subsequence, sum the pointwise norms of its increments, use monotone convergence to obtain an almost-everywhere Cauchy series, and estimate its Lp tail by Minkowski.

references.title: Tomáš Roubíček, Nonlinear Partial Differential Equations with Applications, 2nd ed., Birkhäuser, 2005
references.locator: §1.5, construction of Bochner spaces and completeness

references.title: Haim Brezis, Functional Analysis, Sobolev Spaces and Partial Differential Equations, Springer Universitext, 2011
references.locator: Chapter 4, Bochner integration and Lp completeness, PDF pp. 90–105

items.title: An outward-pointing finite-dimensional map has a zero
items.statement:
Let $N\ge1$, $R>0$, and let $F:\mathbb R^N\to\mathbb R^N$ be continuous.
If $F(x)\cdot x>0$ for every $|x|=R$, then $F$ has a zero in the closed
ball $\overline B_R(0)$.
items.strategy: Normalize −F on the ball to obtain a Brouwer fixed point; a fixed point must lie on the sphere and contradict the outward-pointing inequality.

references.title: Marvin Fritz, Monotone Operators in Nonlinear PDEs, JKU lecture notes, WS 2023/2024
references.locator: Theorem 2.1 and its Galerkin proof, finite-dimensional outward-pointing map step.

references.title: Haim Brezis, Functional Analysis, Sobolev Spaces and Partial Differential Equations, Springer Universitext, 2011
references.locator: Theorem 5.16, finite-dimensional Brouwer argument in the Minty–Browder proof, PDF p. 159.

items.title: Quasi-uniform finite-element mass inverses have summable graph decay
items.strategy: Prove nodal unisolvence and cellwise coefficient scaling, count common-cell graph balls, then use a Neumann series for the scaled mass inverse and sum its geometric-distance bound.
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Fix a degree $k\ge1$. The mesh contract has two
branches. In dimensions $d\ge2$, let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a bounded
polyhedral open set and let $\mathcal T_h$ be finite matching affine
simplex meshes as in [[def-matching-affine-simplicial-meshes]], with
$h=\max_{K\in\mathcal T_h}\operatorname{diam}K$, $h\to0$,
$\operatorname{diam}K\le h$, $\operatorname{diam}K\ge\theta h$, and
$\operatorname{diam}K/\rho_K\le\sigma$ for constants $\theta>0$ and
$\sigma<\infty$ independent of $h$. In dimension $d=1$, let $\Omega$ be a
bounded interval or a finite union of bounded intervals with pairwise
disjoint closures, and let $\mathcal T_h$ be finite interval partitions of
the component closures meeting only at whole endpoints, with interval lengths
between $\theta h$ and $h$ and $h\to0$.

For each mesh, place the degree-$k$ barycentric Lagrange nodes on every
$d\ge2$ simplex, or the $k+1$ equally spaced Lagrange nodes on every
$d=1$ interval, identify coincident nodes of matching cells, and impose zero
coefficients at every node on $\partial\Omega$. Let $V_h$ be the resulting
scalar continuous piecewise-$\mathbb P_k$ space. If $z_i$ are its interior
nodes, $\phi_i$ the global nodal basis, and
$$
M_{ij}=\int_\Omega\phi_i\phi_j,\qquad A_h=h^{-d}M,
$$
join distinct nodes when they occur in one cell and write $\delta_h(i,j)$ for
the shortest path length in this graph (with $\delta_h(i,j)=\infty$ when
there is no path, and use $q^\infty=0$). Whenever $V_h\ne\{0\}$, there are
$a,b,C>0$ and
$q\in(0,1)$, independent of the mesh, such that
$$\operatorname{spec}(A_h)\subset[a,b],\qquad |(A_h^{-1})_{ij}|\le Cq^{\delta_h(i,j)},\qquad \sup_i\sum_j|(A_h^{-1})_{ij}|+\sup_j\sum_i|(A_h^{-1})_{ij}|\le C.$$
For every cell $K$ and $1\le r<\infty$, if $c_K$ are its local nodal
coefficients and $w_h=\sum_{i\in I(K)}c_i\phi_i$ on $K$, then
$$c_r h_K^{d/r}\|c_K\|_{\ell^r}\le\|w_h\|_{L^r(K)}\le C_r h_K^{d/r}\|c_K\|_{\ell^r},\qquad \|\nabla w_h\|_{L^r(K)}\le C_rh_K^{d/r-1}\|c_K\|_{\ell^r}.$$
At $r=\infty$, omit $h_K^{d/r}$ in the function estimate and replace the
gradient bound by
$\|\nabla w_h\|_{L^\infty(K)}\le Ch_K^{-1}\|c_K\|_{\ell^\infty}$.
Summing gives, for all global nodal coefficients including zero boundary
coefficients,
$$c_r h^{d/r}\|c\|_{\ell^r}\le\Big\|\sum_i c_i\phi_i\Big\|_{L^r(\Omega)}\le C_r h^{d/r}\|c\|_{\ell^r}.$$
with the factor $h^{d/r}$ omitted at $r=\infty$. The empty interior-node
case is interpreted as $V_h=\{0\}$ and has no mass matrix to invert.

references.title: Lars Diening, Johannes Storn, and Tabea Tscherpel, On the Sobolev and Lp-Stability of the L2-Projection, arXiv:2008.01801v2
references.locator: §2.2, Lemma 2.1 and Proposition 2.2, PDF pp. 4–5: locality and graph-distance decay for the L2 projection. The present proof gives a separate entrywise Neumann-series argument under global quasi-uniformity.

references.locator: Chapter 12 §12.1, PDF pp. 102–103: nodal finite-element spaces and the L2 projection used in the parabolic Galerkin setting.

items.title: Coercive monotone p-growth diffusion fluxes
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]).

Let $d\ge1$, let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a bounded open set, and
let $1<p<\infty$ satisfy $p>\max(1,2d/(d+2))$. Put
$V=W_0^{1,p}(\Omega;\mathbb R)$ with norm
$\|v\|_V=\|\nabla v\|_{L^p(\Omega)}$, $H=L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R)$, and
$p'=p/(p-1)$. The Poincaré inequality makes this norm equivalent to the full
$W^{1,p}$ norm. [[lem-pe12-w0p-separable-reflexive]] gives separability and
reflexivity, while [[lem-pe12-w1p-compact-l2-embedding]] gives the dense
continuous compact inclusion $V\Subset H$; these are the hypotheses of the
evolution triple in [[def-pe12-gelfand-triple]]. The compact-inclusion result
uses the stated threshold also when $d=1$, where it reduces to $p>1$.

A measurable flux $a:\Omega\times\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R^d$ is an admissible
**coercive monotone diffusion flux of p-growth** if it is Carathéodory (for
each $\xi$, $x\mapsto a(x,\xi)$ is measurable, and for almost every $x$,
$\xi\mapsto a(x,\xi)$ is continuous), and there are constants $C<\infty$,
$\alpha>0$, nonnegative functions $g\in L^{p'}(\Omega)$ and
$h\in L^1(\Omega)$, and one
null set outside which, for all $\xi,\eta\in\mathbb R^d$,
$$|a(x,\xi)|\le C\bigl(g(x)+|\xi|^{p-1}\bigr),\qquad a(x,\xi)\cdot\xi\ge\alpha|\xi|^p-h(x),$$
$$\bigl(a(x,\xi)-a(x,\eta)\bigr)\cdot(\xi-\eta)\ge0.$$
The induced operator $A:V\to V^*$ is
$$\langle A(v),w\rangle_{V^*,V} =\int_\Omega a(x,\nabla v(x))\cdot\nabla w(x)\,dx.$$
The growth bound and Hölder's inequality make this pairing finite and give
$\|A(v)\|_{V^*}\le C_1(\|g\|_{p'}+\|v\|_V^{p-1})$ for a constant $C_1$.
The finite-dimensional test-coordinate continuity used in the backward Euler
existence argument follows from the stated Carathéodory and growth conditions
by dominated convergence, as proved in
[[thm-pe12-backward-euler-galerkin-existence-energy]]. No additional global
operator-continuity hypothesis is imposed.

For $f\in L^{p'}(0,T;V^*)$, a weak evolution solution is a function
$u\in W_p(0,T;V)\cap L^\infty(0,T;H)$ with a continuous $H$ representative
such that $u'+A(u)=f$ in $L^{p'}(0,T;V^*)$ and $u(0)=u_0\in H$.
items.strategy: State the exact pointwise hypotheses that make the variational flux well-defined, p-growth bounded, coercive and monotone.

references.title: Marvin Fritz, Monotone Operators in Nonlinear PDEs, JKU lecture notes, WS 2023/2024
references.locator: §§3–4, especially the Nemytskii and quasilinear elliptic flux hypotheses, PDF pp. 10–17

references.title: Haim Brezis, Functional Analysis, Sobolev Spaces and Partial Differential Equations, Springer Universitext, 2011
references.locator: Theorem 5.16 (Minty–Browder), PDF p. 159; Chapter 9, Sobolev spaces and Rellich compactness

items.title: Conforming FEM families with stable L2 projectors
items.statement:
Let $(V,H,J)$ be the Banach evolution triple of
[[def-pe12-gelfand-triple]]. An **admissible stable conforming FEM sequence**
consists of finite-dimensional subspaces $V_k\subset V$ and their
$H$-orthogonal projections $\Pi_k:H\to V_k$ such that:

1. $\Pi_k(V)\subset V$, $\Pi_kv=v$ for $v\in V_k$, and
   $(w_k,z-\Pi_kz)_H=0$ for every $w_k\in V_k$, $z\in H$;
2. $\sup_k\|\Pi_k\|_{V\to V}\le C_\Pi<\infty$ and
   $\Pi_kv\to v$ in $V$ for each $v\in V$;
3. the associated time partitions of $[0,T]$ have maximum step
   $\delta_k\to0$.

The convergence in clause 2 and density of $V$ in $H$ imply
$\Pi_kz\to z$ in $H$ for every $z\in H$: use
$\|\Pi_k(z-v)\|_H\le\|z-v\|_H$, $\Pi_kv\to v$ in $H$, and approximate $z$
by $v\in V$. Thus the range spaces approximate every $H$ vector.

For a fixed $k$, backward Euler with averages $f_k^n$ uses unknowns
$U_k^n\in V_k$ and equations
$$\left(\frac{U_k^n-U_k^{n-1}}{\tau_n},v_k\right)_H +\langle A(U_k^n),v_k\rangle =\langle f_k^n,v_k\rangle\qquad(v_k\in V_k).$$
Its piecewise-constant reconstruction is $\overline U_k(t)=U_k^n$ on
$(t_{n-1},t_n]$; its affine reconstruction joins $U_k^{n-1}$ to $U_k^n$.
items.strategy: Make the exact spatial projection and mesh-density interface used to lift the finite-dimensional time derivative into V* explicit.

references.title: Christian Clason, Introduction to Finite Element Methods, lecture notes, arXiv:1709.08618v2
references.locator: Chapter 12 §§12.1–12.2, PDF pp. 102–105: conforming spatial subspaces and the L2 projection

items.title: The Banach evolution-space energy identity and H trace
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let
$(V,H,J)$ be the Banach evolution triple of
[[def-pe12-gelfand-triple]], let $1<p<\infty$, and suppose
$u\in L^p(0,T;V)$ with distributional derivative
$u'\in L^{p'}(0,T;V^*)$. Then $u$ has a unique representative in
$C([0,T];H)$ and, for every $0\le s\le t\le T$,
$$\|u(t)\|_H^2-\|u(s)\|_H^2 =2\int_s^t\langle u'(r),u(r)\rangle_{V^*,V}\,dr.$$
items.strategy: Mollify on interior intervals, pass the scalar norm derivative to L1, then use scalar pairings, density of V in H, Riesz representation and norm continuity to construct the strong H trace.

references.title: Tomáš Roubíček, Nonlinear Partial Differential Equations with Applications, 2nd ed., Birkhäuser, 2005
references.locator: §7.2, norm chain rule and continuous H-valued representative, printed pp. 205–207

references.title: Christian Clason, Introduction to Finite Element Methods, lecture notes, arXiv:1709.08618v2
references.locator: Chapter 11 §11.1, PDF pp. 96–98, evolution-space trace and energy identity

items.title: Aubin–Lions compactness with exact time exponent
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let
$(V,H,J)$ be a Banach evolution triple with compact inclusion
$i:V\Subset H$ and continuous canonical inclusion $J:H\hookrightarrow V^*$.
Let $T<\infty$, $1<p<\infty$, and $1<q\le\infty$. Suppose
$u_j\in L^p(0,T;V)$ have distributional derivatives
$u_j'\in L^q(0,T;V^*)$ and
$$\sup_j\bigl(\|u_j\|_{L^p(0,T;V)}+\|u_j'\|_{L^q(0,T;V^*)}\bigr)<\infty.$$
Then $(u_j)$ is relatively compact in $L^p(0,T;H)$. If also
$\sup_j\|u_j\|_{L^\infty(0,T;H)}<\infty$, each subsequence converging in
$L^p(0,T;H)$ converges, after the same subsequence, in every
$L^r(0,T;H)$ with $1\le r<\infty$.
items.strategy: Approximate the V unit ball by finite-dimensional H subspaces, control coefficients by the V* derivative, use finite-dimensional equicontinuity and send the H approximation error to zero.

references.title: Tomáš Roubíček, Nonlinear Partial Differential Equations with Applications, 2nd ed., Birkhäuser, 2005
references.locator: §7.3, Lemma 7.7 and complete proof, printed pp. 208–210

references.title: Marvin Fritz, Monotone Operators in Nonlinear PDEs, JKU lecture notes, WS 2023/2024
references.locator: Theorem 8.8 and Corollary 8.9.1, PDF pp. 33–36

items.title: Weak compactness of bounded space-time Sobolev gradients
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let
$\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ be bounded and open, $d\ge1$, let
$1<p<\infty$, and let $0<T<\infty$. Put $V=W_0^{1,p}(\Omega;\mathbb R)$ with gradient norm
$\|v\|_V=\|\nabla v\|_{L^p}$, and suppose $V$ has a continuous inclusion in
a real Hilbert space $H$. If $u_j$ is bounded in $L^p(0,T;V)$ and its image
in $L^p(0,T;H)$ converges strongly to $u$, then a subsequence converges
weakly in $L^p(0,T;V)$ to some $U$, the image of $U$ equals $u$, and
$\nabla u_j\rightharpoonup\nabla U$ in
$L^p((0,T)\times\Omega;\mathbb R^d)$.
items.strategy: Embed the zero-extended function and its spatial gradient into a finite product of scalar Lp spaces, extract a weak limit, pass the distributional derivative identity, and recover zero trace on the C1 boundary.

references.title: Haim Brezis, Functional Analysis, Sobolev Spaces and Partial Differential Equations, Springer Universitext, 2011
references.locator: Chapter 3 §§3.5–3.6, Theorems 3.18–3.19 and Proposition 3.20, printed pp. 69–73; Chapter 4 §4.3, Theorem 4.10, printed pp. 96–98.

references.title: Tomáš Roubíček, Nonlinear Partial Differential Equations with Applications, 2nd ed., Birkhäuser, 2005
references.locator: §7.3, Lemma 7.7 and proof, printed pp. 208–210, for the compactness-and-weak-limit route.

items.title: Piecewise-constant discrete Aubin–Lions compactness
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice.

Let $V\Subset H\hookrightarrow V^*$ be a Banach evolution triple. For each
$k$, let $0=t_0^k<\cdots<t_{N_k}^k=T$ be a partition with maximum step
$\delta_k\to0$, let $U_k^n\in V$, and define $\overline U_k(t)=U_k^n$ on
$I_n^k=(t_{n-1}^k,t_n^k]$ and
$D_k(t)=(U_k^n-U_k^{n-1})/\tau_n^k$ there. Suppose, for some
$1<p<\infty$ and $1<q\le\infty$,
$$\sup_k\|\overline U_k\|_{L^p(0,T;V)} +\sup_k\|D_k\|_{L^q(0,T;V^*)}<\infty.$$
Then the time translates satisfy, on their common intervals,
$$\|\overline U_k(\cdot+s)-\overline U_k\|_{L^q(V^*)} \le (s+2\delta_k)\|D_k\|_{L^q(V^*)},$$
and $(\overline U_k)$ is relatively compact in $L^p(0,T;H)$. If also
$\sup_{k,n}\|U_k^n\|_H<\infty$, every convergent subsequence converges in
every $L^r(0,T;H)$ with $1\le r<\infty$.
items.strategy: Compare the piecewise-constant reconstruction with its affine interpolant, prove an O(δk) reconstruction defect and O(h+δk) V* translates, then use the same finite-rank compact approximation.

references.title: Tomáš Roubíček, Nonlinear Partial Differential Equations with Applications, 2nd ed., Birkhäuser, 2005
references.locator: §7.3, compactness proof via time averaging, printed pp. 208–210

references.title: Christian Clason, Introduction to Finite Element Methods, lecture notes, arXiv:1709.08618v2
references.locator: Chapter 12 §12.1, piecewise-constant dG(0)/implicit Euler time stepping, PDF pp. 102–103

items.title: Boundary-preserving quasi-interpolation is stable and strongly approximating
items.strategy: Convolve the zero extension, sample only interior Lagrange nodes, prove local cube Poincare estimates and boundary exterior density, and obtain strong convergence by smooth-density and uniform stability.
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Use either mesh branch and the nodal space defined
in [[lem-pe12-quasiuniform-mass-inverse-decay]]. For $d\ge2$, assume
$\Omega$ is a bounded polyhedral open set whose boundary is locally a graph
of a Lipschitz function with $\Omega$ on one side; for $d=1$, use a bounded
nonempty interval or a finite nonempty union of bounded intervals with
pairwise disjoint closures. Let $1\le p<\infty$. There is a linear map
$$
Q_h:W_0^{1,p}(\Omega)\longrightarrow V_h
$$
with the following construction. Fix a nonnegative $\rho\in C_c^\infty(B(0,1))$
with $\int\rho=1$, let $E_0$ be extension by zero, and set
$S_hv=\rho_h*E_0v$ with $\rho_h(x)=h^{-d}\rho(x/h)$. The degree-$k$
coefficient of $Q_hv$ at every interior node $z$ is $S_hv(z)$; every
boundary-node coefficient is zero. For all sufficiently fine meshes,
$$\|v-Q_hv\|_{L^p(\Omega)}\le Ch\|\nabla v\|_{L^p(\Omega)},\qquad \|\nabla Q_hv\|_{L^p(\Omega)}\le C\|\nabla v\|_{L^p(\Omega)}.$$
Consequently $Q_hv\to v$ in $W^{1,p}(\Omega)$ for each
$v\in W_0^{1,p}(\Omega)$. Constants are uniform over the fixed mesh family
and may depend on $d,k,p,\Omega,\theta,\sigma$ and $\rho$. The operator
$Q_h$ is not asserted to be a projector.

references.title: Lars Diening, Johannes Storn, and Tabea Tscherpel, On the Sobolev and Lp-Stability of the L2-Projection, arXiv:2008.01801v2
references.locator: §4.3–4.4, PDF pp. 24–25: zero-boundary L2-projector stability and its use of approximation operators. Their Scott–Zhang operator is not imported; the local mollified construction below is proved directly.

references.title: Christian Clason, Introduction to Finite Element Methods, arXiv:1709.08618v2
references.locator: Chapter 12 §12.1, PDF pp. 102–103: conforming finite-element spaces and the associated L2 projection.

items.title: Minty identification for a monotone Carathéodory flux
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice.

Let $Q=(0,T)\times\Omega$ have finite measure, $1<p<\infty$, and let
$a(x,\xi)$ be a Carathéodory flux with the monotonicity and $p$-growth
hypotheses of [[def-pe12-monotone-diffusion-flux]], independent of time.
Suppose $\xi_n\rightharpoonup\xi$ in $L^p(Q;\mathbb R^d)$,
$q_n=a(x,\xi_n)\rightharpoonup q$ in $L^{p'}(Q;\mathbb R^d)$, and
$$\limsup_{n\to\infty}\int_Q q_n\cdot\xi_n \le\int_Qq\cdot\xi.$$
Then $q(x,t)=a(x,\xi(x,t))$ for almost every $(t,x)\in Q$.
items.strategy: Integrate the pointwise monotonicity inequality against arbitrary comparison gradients, pass to the limsup, then test with ∇u±ε∇w and use dominated convergence and hemicontinuity.

references.title: Haim Brezis, Functional Analysis, Sobolev Spaces and Partial Differential Equations, Springer Universitext, 2011
references.locator: Theorem 5.16, Minty–Browder monotonicity argument, PDF p. 159 (printed p. 145).

references.title: Marvin Fritz, Monotone Operators in Nonlinear PDEs, JKU lecture notes, WS 2023/2024
references.locator: §0, Minty trick, PDF pp. 2–3.

items.title: Quantitative residual error under strong monotonicity
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice.

Let $(V,H,J)$ be the evolution triple of
[[def-pe12-gelfand-triple]], $1<p<\infty$, and assume
$A:V\to V^*$ is strongly monotone with constant $\mu>0$ and exponent $p$:
$$\langle A(x)-A(y),x-y\rangle\ge\mu\|x-y\|_V^p \qquad(x,y\in V).$$
Suppose $u,v\in L^p(0,T;V)$ have derivatives in
$L^{p'}(0,T;V^*)$ and residual difference
$R=(u'+A(u))-(v'+A(v))\in L^{p'}(0,T;V^*)$. Then for every $t\in[0,T]$,
$$\|u(t)-v(t)\|_H^2+ \mu\int_0^t\|u-v\|_V^p \le\|u(0)-v(0)\|_H^2+ 2C_{\mu,p}\|R\|_{L^{p'}(0,t;V^*)}^{p'},$$
where both functions use their continuous $H$ representatives and
$C_{\mu,p}=\frac1{p'}(2/(\mu p))^{1/(p-1)}$. In particular, equal initial data
and zero residual imply $u=v$.
items.strategy: Subtract the weak equations, test by the solution difference, apply the energy chain rule and p/p′ Young inequality, then integrate.

references.title: Tomáš Roubíček, Nonlinear Partial Differential Equations with Applications, 2nd ed., Birkhäuser, 2005
references.locator: §7.2, evolution-space energy chain rule and monotone uniqueness framework.

references.title: Marvin Fritz, Monotone Operators in Nonlinear PDEs, JKU lecture notes, WS 2023/2024

items.title: L2 projections are uniformly W1p-stable on quasi-uniform conforming meshes
items.strategy: Use scaled mass inverse row and column bounds for Lr stability, then combine the boundary-preserving quasi-interpolant, the polynomial inverse inequality, and density for W1p stability and convergence.
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice and fix a degree $k\ge1$. Take a sequence of meshes
with $h\to0$ in either branch and use the
zero-boundary Lagrange spaces $V_h$ from
[[lem-pe12-quasiuniform-mass-inverse-decay]]: globally quasi-uniform,
shape-regular matching affine simplices on a bounded Lipschitz polyhedral
open set in $d\ge2$ (with the local graph-chart convention of
[[lem-pe12-boundary-preserving-quasi-interpolation]]), or interval
partitions of a nonempty bounded interval (or a finite nonempty union of
intervals with disjoint closures) in $d=1$. For $f\in L^1(\Omega)$ define
$P_hf\in V_h$ by the finite mass system
$$
\int_\Omega (P_hf)w_h=\int_\Omega fw_h\qquad(w_h\in V_h).
$$
This is well-defined, agrees on $L^2(\Omega)$ with the $L^2$-orthogonal
projection, and is the identity on $V_h$. There are constants independent
of $h$ such that
$$\|P_hf\|_{L^r(\Omega)}\le C_r\|f\|_{L^r(\Omega)}\qquad(1\le r\le\infty).$$
For every $1<p<\infty$ and $v\in W_0^{1,p}(\Omega)$,
$$\|\nabla P_hv\|_{L^p(\Omega)}\le C_p\|\nabla v\|_{L^p(\Omega)},\qquad P_hv\longrightarrow v\quad\text{in }W^{1,p}(\Omega).$$
For the PE12 application, additionally assume the Axiom of Choice and
$p>\max(1,2d/(d+2))$. The compact embedding
[[lem-pe12-w1p-compact-l2-embedding]] makes $V=W_0^{1,p}(\Omega)$ a dense
subspace of $H=L^2(\Omega)$, and
[[lem-pe12-w0p-separable-reflexive]] supplies the separable reflexive Banach
structure. Thus these spaces form the evolution triple of
[[def-pe12-monotone-diffusion-flux]] and
[[def-pe12-gelfand-triple]], and the $P_h$ above is its $H$-orthogonal
projector. Together with any time partitions whose maximum step tends to
zero it satisfies the projector clauses in
[[def-pe12-stable-conforming-fem-family]]. For every $d\ge2$, the uniform
Kuhn/Freudenthal meshes of $\Omega=(0,1)^d$, and for $d=1$ the uniform
interval meshes of $\Omega=(0,1)$, are explicit nonempty instances throughout
that full strict $p$ range. Time refinement is independent of spatial
refinement.

references.title: Lars Diening, Johannes Storn, and Tabea Tscherpel, On the Sobolev and Lp-Stability of the L2-Projection, arXiv:2008.01801v2
references.locator: §2.2, Proposition 2.2, and §4.4, Theorem 4.14 with complete proof, PDF pp. 4–5 and 24–25. The paper treats its stated mesh-grading conditions; this carrier proves the global quasi-uniform branches below directly.

references.locator: Chapter 12 §12.1, PDF pp. 102–103: the finite-element L2 projection and parabolic method-of-lines context.

items.title: Nonlinear backward Euler Galerkin existence and energy bounds
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice.

Assume the hypotheses in [[def-pe12-monotone-diffusion-flux]] and an
admissible stable conforming FEM sequence
$(V_k,\Pi_k,\mathcal P_k)$ from
[[def-pe12-stable-conforming-fem-family]]. Let
$f\in L^{p'}(0,T;V^*)$, $u_0\in H$, and on each partition
$\mathcal P_k=(I_k^n)_{n=1}^{N_k}$ put
$f_k^n=|I_k^n|^{-1}\int_{I_k^n}f(t)\,dt$ and
$U_k^0=\Pi_ku_0$. Then for each $k$ there exist
$U_k^n\in V_k$, $1\le n\le N_k$, satisfying
$$\left(\frac{U_k^n-U_k^{n-1}}{\tau_k^n},v_k\right)_H +\langle A(U_k^n),v_k\rangle =\langle f_k^n,v_k\rangle\qquad(v_k\in V_k).$$
Every such solution obeys a bound, independent of $k$ and the time steps,
on
$$\max_n\|U_k^n\|_H^2+ \sum_n\|U_k^n-U_k^{n-1}\|_H^2+ \sum_n\tau_k^n\|U_k^n\|_V^p+ \|D_k\|_{L^{p'}(0,T;V^*)}^{p'},$$
where $D_k=(U_k^n-U_k^{n-1})/\tau_k^n$ on $I_k^n$. The bound depends only
on the flux constants, $p$, $T$, the family stability constant
$C_\Pi$, $\|u_0\|_H$, $\|f\|_{L^{p'}(V^*)}$,
$\|g\|_{L^{p'}(\Omega)}$, and $\|h\|_{L^1(\Omega)}$.

In particular, the same existence and energy conclusion holds on the
fixed-degree uniform interval meshes of $(0,1)$ in $d=1$ and uniform
Kuhn/Freudenthal simplex meshes of $(0,1)^d$ for $d\ge2$, paired with any
time partitions whose maximum step tends to zero independently of the
spatial mesh.
items.strategy: Apply the outward-pointing Brouwer lemma at each step, test with the new solution, use the Hilbert discrete energy identity, coercivity and conjugate-exponent Young inequality.

items.title: Conditional monotone finite-element convergence
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $d\ge1$, let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^d$ be
a bounded open set, let $1<p<\infty$ satisfy
$p>\max(1,2d/(d+2))$, and let $T>0$. Let $V=W_0^{1,p}(\Omega;\mathbb R)$
with gradient norm, $H=L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R)$, and let
$a(x,\xi)$ satisfy [[def-pe12-monotone-diffusion-flux]]. Assume an admissible
stable conforming FEM sequence $(V_k,\Pi_k,\mathcal P_k)$ from
[[def-pe12-stable-conforming-fem-family]]. For $f\in L^{p'}(0,T;V^*)$ and
$u_0\in H$, set $f_k^n=|I_k^n|^{-1}\int_{I_k^n}f$ and $U_k^0=\Pi_ku_0$.
For each $k$, let $(U_k^n)$ be any solution of the backward Euler equations
in [[thm-pe12-backward-euler-galerkin-existence-energy]].

There are a subsequence, still indexed by $k$, and a unique
$u\in L^p(0,T;V)\cap L^\infty(0,T;H)\cap C([0,T];H)$ such that
$$\overline U_k\to u\quad\text{strongly in }L^r(0,T;H) \text{ for every }1\le r<\infty,\qquad \overline U_k\rightharpoonup u\text{ in }L^p(0,T;V),$$
the fluxes $a(x,\nabla\overline U_k)$ converge weakly in
$L^{p'}((0,T)\times\Omega;\mathbb R^d)$ to $a(x,\nabla u)$, and
$$u'+A(u)=f\quad\text{in }L^{p'}(0,T;V^*),\qquad u(0)=u_0.$$
Existence of each discrete solution and uniform energy bounds are included
in [[thm-pe12-backward-euler-galerkin-existence-energy]]. The abstract
convergence claim is conditional on the FEM projector clauses. For
$\Omega=(0,1)$ in $d=1$ and $\Omega=(0,1)^d$ in each $d\ge2$, the explicit
fixed-degree interval and Kuhn/Freudenthal simplex families of
[[thm-pe12-l2-projector-w1p-stability]] verify those clauses for any
independent time partitions with vanishing maximum step. These are concrete
nonempty instances of the theorem on the full approved strict $p$ range.
items.strategy: Use the energy bound, projected discrete derivative estimate and discrete Aubin–Lions compactness; pass the weak equation and initial trace, derive the Minty limsup from the discrete energy identity, identify the flux, and prove uniqueness by the chain rule.

title: Nonlinear parabolic compactness and monotone evolution — Examples

items.title: A Barenblatt profile has finite propagation
items.statement:
For $m>1$ and $C>0$, put
$$\beta=\frac1{m+1},\qquad k=\frac{m-1}{2m(m+1)},\qquad u(t,x)=t^{-\beta} \left(C-kx^2t^{-2\beta}\right)_+^{1/(m-1)} \quad(t>0,\ x\in\mathbb R),$$
where $r_+=\max(r,0)$. Then $u$ is a nonnegative distributional solution
of the one-dimensional porous-medium equation
$u_t=(u^m)_{xx}$ on $(0,\infty)\times\mathbb R$. For every $t>0$ it is
supported in
$$|x|\le\sqrt{C/k}\,t^{1/(m+1)},$$
so its support radius is finite and grows like $t^{1/(m+1)}$.
items.strategy: Differentiate the positive-part self-similar profile in its positivity region, match the scaling exponents and coefficient, then verify the flux has no boundary delta and compute the support.

items.title: The linear Ritz projection need not preserve the nonlinear p-Laplacian residual
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. On $\Omega=(0,1)$, let
$V=H_0^1(0,1;\mathbb R)$ with the full $H^1$ norm, let
$H=L^2(0,1;\mathbb R)$, and use their canonical evolution triple. Let
$w(x)=2x$ on $[0,1/2]$ and $w(x)=2(1-x)$ on $[1/2,1]$, and set
$V_h=\operatorname{span}\{w\}$. Use the coercive symmetric form
$a(f,g)=\int_0^1 f'g'\,dx$ for the Ritz projection, and let
$v(x)=x(1-x)$. For the nonlinear $3$-Laplacian flux $J_3(s)=|s|s$,
$$\int_0^1 |(R_hv)'|(R_hv)'w'\,dx=\frac12 \ne\frac23=\int_0^1|v'|v'w'\,dx.$$
Thus the linear Ritz projection does not in general preserve the nonlinear
$p$-Laplacian Galerkin residual.
items.strategy: Use Ω=(0,1), the two-element P1 space, u(x)=x(1−x) and p=3; compute both residual pairings against the midpoint hat function and compare 1/2 with 2/3.

items.title: Time oscillations defeat compactness without derivative control
items.statement:
Let $(V,H,J)$ be a Banach evolution triple, let $T>0$, and fix
$0\ne v\in V$. For each positive integer $n$, define
$$u_n(t)=\sin(2\pi nt/T)\,v.$$
Then $(u_n)$ is bounded in $L^p(0,T;V)$ for every $1\le p<\infty$, but it
has no strongly convergent subsequence in $L^2(0,T;H)$. Its time-derivative
norm grows linearly in $n$ in every $L^q(0,T;V^*)$, $1\le q\le\infty$.
items.strategy: Take distinct integer temporal frequencies multiplying one fixed nonzero V vector; orthogonality gives a uniform positive pairwise L2(H) distance while the L2(V) norms stay constant.

items.title: The p-Laplacian is an admissible monotone diffusion
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a nonempty
bounded open set, $d\ge1$, and let $p>\max(1,2d/(d+2))$. The flux
$a(x,\xi)=|\xi|^{p-2}\xi$, with $a(x,0)=0$, satisfies the coercivity,
monotonicity and $p$-growth hypotheses in
[[def-pe12-monotone-diffusion-flux]], and its induced operator is additionally norm-continuous. Its zero-boundary space embeds
compactly into $L^2(\Omega)$. In particular, on the nonempty interval
$\Omega=(0,1)$ for $d=1$, or the nonempty unit cube $\Omega=(0,1)^d$ for
$d\ge2$, the explicit fixed-degree interval or Kuhn/Freudenthal meshes and
any independent time partitions with vanishing maximum step satisfy the
projector hypotheses. The convergence theorem
[[thm-pe12-monotone-fem-limit]] therefore applies on those concrete meshes
for every load and initial datum in its stated classes; no projector
condition remains outstanding in this example.
items.strategy: Identify a as the gradient of the convex function |ξ|^p/p, verify its growth and coercivity, and invoke the proved Sobolev embedding and convergence theorem.
